title: Rushing and copying tripwire
scenario: Scan one batch of ticket-summary submissions for rushing (duration below 25% of the task median) and copying (same normalised answer as another annotator on the same task), then flag annotators and pick the worst rusher.

verified.why_correct: The `//` only computes the middle index, which must be an integer. The even case divides the sum of the two middle values with `/`, so t2 correctly gives 112.5. It looks like the integer-division suspect but it is fine.

bugs.title: Rush rate floored by integer division
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_rush_rates: A02 shows 33 instead of 33.3, and every rate comes back as a whole number (0, 50) rather than a float. Flags and worst_rusher are unchanged.
bugs.why: `100 * rushed // timed` floors to a whole percentage before round() runs, so 1 of 3 becomes 33 instead of 33.3. Rates that divide evenly (0, 50) look fine, which hides it.
hints: Only A02's rate is off, and only in the decimals. What is special about 1 of 3?
Look at how rush_rate is computed in timing.py.
`100 * rushed // timed` floors; use `/` so round(..., 1) has a fraction to round.
probes: Why did A03 and A05 (2 of 4) come out right with the floor?
Why is the `//` in median() fine while this one isn't?

bugs.title: Own submission ends the twin search
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_shared_answer_counts: A04 and A08 get 2 shared answers each instead of 4, and A01 drops out (0 instead of 1). The copying flags stay the same, so Test 2 still passes.
bugs.why: The task's submission list includes the submission itself. Returning False when the loop reaches the annotator's own row stops the search, so whoever answered first on a task never sees the later identical answer.
hints: A04 and A08 share four answers, yet each gets credit for only two. Which two, in file order?
Look at what has_twin does when it reaches a submission by the same annotator.
The own-annotator check returns False; it should `continue` to the next submission.
probes: Why did A04 lose t1 and t2 but keep t3 and t4?
Why didn't the copying flags change even though the counts did?

bugs.title: Worst-rusher tie goes to first seen
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_worst_rusher: returns A05 instead of A03. Both have rush_rate 50.0.
bugs.why: max() returns the first annotator to reach the top rate, and `rush` is ordered by first submission in the file, not by id. A05 submits before A03, so the 50.0 tie goes to A05 instead of the lowest id.
hints: Two annotators share the highest rush rate. Which one does the spec want?
Look at how worst_rusher picks between equal rates, and what order its input is in.
probes: Would this have passed if worst_rusher were given the `rows` dict instead of `rush`? Why?
What does max() do with equal keys?

context_qa.q: What does build_report() call, in order?
context_qa.a: `load_active_annotators` returns sorted active ids, `load_submissions` reads and filters the log, `task_medians` and `rush_stats` build the timing numbers, `shared_answer_counts` builds the copying counts, and then each active annotator gets a row with `flags_for`. The summary is built from those rows, except `worst_rusher`, which is given the `rush` dict.

Rows whose normalised annotator id isn't in the active list, and rows whose parsed `submitted_at` is before `BATCH_START` (2026-04-01). Blank answers and blank durations are kept; a blank duration becomes `None`.

context_qa.q: What order are the keys in the dict returned by rush_stats?
context_qa.a: It is a defaultdict filled while walking the submissions in file order, so keys appear in the order each annotator's first timed submission appears. Annotators with no timed submissions are not in it.

context_qa.q: What does has_twin receive as same_task?
context_qa.a: The full list of counted submissions for that task, in file order, built in `shared_answer_counts`. That list includes the submission being checked.
It strips, lower-cases, replaces runs of whitespace with one space, then strips trailing `.` and `!` characters and any whitespace left behind. A blank answer gives an empty key.

context_qa.q: How is a task median computed when a task has an even number of timed submissions?
context_qa.a: `median` sorts the values, takes `mid = len // 2`, and for an even count returns the sum of the two middle values divided by 2.
